subject: The farm is yours
body:
My dear sprout,

If you're reading this, you've found the old place. I'm sorry about the weeds. My knees gave out long before the soil did.

The farm is yours now. Bramblewick could use a farmer again: the mill is quiet, the market's shuttered, and the road is half buried in rocks. Start small. A few radishes never hurt anyone.

Goldie at the store will look in on you. Tell her I said she still owes me a pie.

With love and dirt under my nails,
Tobias

subject: About that gate
body:
Hello neighbour,

Goldie tells me Tobias's gate finally fell off its hinges. I can rebuild it, and open up the field behind it while I'm at it.

Bring me 4 wood, 3 stone and 60 coins. Branches and rocks around your farm will do nicely.

Bruno

subject: Your gate is up!
body:
Morning!

Worked through the night. The new gate swings like a dream, and the back field is yours to clear. Mind the rocks.

Bruno

P.S. Goldie says she'll pay well for anything you grow out there.

subject: About old Rufus
body:
Hello dear,

You've done wonders with that farm. Now I need a favour.

Rufus ran the mill until the wheel jammed. He's been sulking up there ever since. He'll say he doesn't want help. He does.

He'll be by your gate. Be patient with him.

Goldie

subject: The wheel turns
body:
Farmer,

I heard it this morning before I even opened my eyes. That creak. That splash. Twenty years I've waited for that sound.

The mill is yours to use. Bring wheat, take flour. No charge. Don't make it weird.

Rufus

subject: I heard about the mill
body:
My dear sprout,

News travels up the valley faster than the river. The mill is turning again! Rufus wrote to me himself, and he hasn't written to anyone since 1998.

Next, the market square. Bramblewick used to fill it every Saturday. Someone there still bakes the best bread in the valley, if only she had the flour.

Proud of you,
Tobias

subject: THE MARKET IS OPEN
body:
Dear farmer,

I walked through the square at sunrise and every stall was standing. There's bunting! Bruno even painted my stall pink. I didn't ask for pink. I love the pink.

Opening day is today. I have absolutely nothing ready. Please come by.

Pip

P.S. Sorry about the capital letters in the subject.

subject: About my seed collection
body:
My dear sprout,

A market again! Pip wrote to me in three colours of ink.

Ziggy tells me Dr. Hazel Quill is coming to Bramblewick. She and I traded seeds for forty years, and I left her my whole collection: every crop I ever grew, written down in a battered old almanac.

Help her finish it. She'll pretend she doesn't need help. She does.

With love,
Tobias

subject: I'm coming home
body:
My dear sprout,

Hazel wrote to me. Hazel, who has not admitted I was right about anything since 1981, wrote to say I was right about the golden melons.

I'm coming home for the harvest. My knees and I have agreed on one last trip up the valley.

Grow me something golden, and we'll throw a festival the whole of Bramblewick will remember.

With all my love,
Tobias

subject: Thank you
body:
My dear sprout,

What a festival. Rufus danced. Rufus! Pip baked forty pies and sold forty-one, which she says is a mystery. Ziggy gave a speech nobody asked for. Moss ate a whole melon rind and looked very pleased with himself.

Bruno and Juniper made you something. It's waiting by your fence. Please don't make me look at it too often; I'm told it looks just like me.

The farm is yours, and so is the valley, in a way. Keep growing things.

With all my love, always,
Tobias

subject: About leaving
body:
My dear sprout,

I've unpacked. I meant to stay a week, and then Pip offered me the room above the bakery, and the bread smells like 1975, and here we are.

I went down to the creek this morning. The old dock where I used to fish with Nell Brightwater has rotted clean through. Nell still keeps the river from her houseboat on the far bank. She's been ferrying people across since before you were born, and she has not forgiven me for leaving.

If you fixed the dock, she might ferry you across. She might even teach you to fish. She taught me, though she'd say it didn't take.

Bruno will know what it needs.

With all my love,
Tobias

subject: The far bank
body:
My dear sprout,

Nell ferried me across yesterday. First time in forty years. She didn't say a word the whole way, and then on the far bank she said, "Took you long enough," and I'm choosing to believe she meant it kindly.

My old seed shed is still standing over there. The roof is mostly sky, but the bench is there, and the jars. This is where I crossed seeds when I was young and certain about everything.

Hazel says what I did in that shed was 'enthusiastic, not scientific'. She also asked if she could see it. Twice.

I'll write again when I've swept out the spiders.

With all my love,
Tobias

subject: I've rewritten the Almanac!
body:
Dear farmer,

I spent last night scraping jam off Tobias's almanac and found whole chapters underneath. He knew a great deal more than he let on.

From now on, each time a crop earns a star you can pick from three new kinds of mastery as well as coins and XP:

Quick Growth: the crop ripens a little sooner.
Bountiful: a better chance of an extra crop at harvest.
Thrifty: cheaper seeds.

And because nobody chooses perfectly the first time, once a week you may redo one crop's stars. Find it on that crop's page.

Your first redo is ready now, in case you'd like to rethink the stars you've already earned.

With fewer jam stains,
Hazel

subject: A gold page
body:
Dear farmer,

One of your crops has reached its tenth star. In all my years I've only given a handful of gold-leaf pages, and Tobias got none of them. (Don't tell him.)

Look for the gold border in the Almanac, and keep an eye on your field when that crop ripens. It's earned a little sparkle.

Proudly,
Hazel

subject: My old notebook
body:
My dear sprout,

Goldie tells me you filled her carrot order. Carrot cake! She hasn't baked that since I left.

I forgot to tell you: my old farming notebook is on the shelf in the barn. It's dog-eared and there's jam on most of it, but most of it is still true. You'll find it in your menu from now on.

The pages fill in as you go. I never wrote anything down before I needed it.

With love,
Tobias

P.S. The crate is for when you're in a hurry. Neighbours always pay better.

subject: Found something in the rubble
body:
Morning, neighbour.

The crew went back over the rubble from all those boulders we cleared for you. Turns out we'd been tossing gold nuggets in with the stone. Embarrassing. My cousin says I need glasses. My cousin is wrong.

I've put what we found in your barn. From now on, about one boulder in ten has a nugget, and we'll hand it straight over.

Bruno

subject: Tobias's pickle crocks
body:
Hello, dear!

I was tidying my cellar and found Tobias's old pickle crocks, still smelling faintly of dill. He used to bring me a jar of pickled radishes every autumn.

Bring me 12 radishes and 6 carrots and I'll start a crock of each, the way he showed me. I've pinned it on the Board.

Goldie

subject: The crocks need a home
body:
Dear,

The crocks are bubbling away nicely. But they're far too heavy for my little store, and pickles want a cool, dark spot.

I asked Bruno to build you proper shelves on the farm. He's pinned what he needs on the Board: wood and stone, the usual.

Goldie

subject: Your Pickling Station
body:
Dear,

Bruno's shelves are up, and the crocks are yours now. Come and look: the first jar of pickled radishes is ready on the shelf.

Here's how it's done. Tap the Pickling Station, choose what to pickle, and leave it. Pickles take a few hours, so start a crock before bed and it'll be ready in the morning.

Tobias always said patience is the secret ingredient. I always said it was salt.

Goldie

subject: Grandma's loom
body:
Hi!

You're growing cotton now? Then you need my grandma's loom. It's been sitting in the corner of my studio under a pile of canvases.

Bruno says he can move it to your farm and fix it up. Ask him in Town. Thread is quick, cloth takes a while, and a quilt takes all night. I'll show you the quilt pattern when we know each other better.

Juniper

subject: A recipe card for you
body:
Dear,

I've copied out my carrot cake recipe for you. Six carrots, two scoops of flour, and a bakery that's warm. Tobias asked for it every birthday.

It's in your bakery now. Don't tell Pip I gave it away.

Goldie

subject: Corn relish
body:
Neighbour,

The crew lives on my corn relish. Three ears of corn and a tomato, and six hours in a crock. I wrote it on the back of an invoice. Don't pay the invoice.

It's on your Pickling Station now.

Bruno

subject: Pumpkin pie!!
body:
Hello! It's Pip.

You've been so kind that I'm giving you my pumpkin pie recipe. One pumpkin, two flour. That's it. That's the secret. There is no other secret. Okay, there's a pinch of something, but I can't tell you.

It's in your bakery now.

Pip

subject: The quilt pattern
body:
Hi!

As promised: Grandma's patchwork quilt pattern. Five cotton and a whole night on the loom. It's slow, but it's the most beautiful thing you'll ever make. And it sells for a lot, which Grandma would want me to mention.

It's on your loom now.

Juniper
